dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission asserts, “28 May has a larger generation gap,” but cites no file, field, timestamp, or calculation.
The claim that this “proves” lower availability is unsupported by the supplied comparison design.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission jumps from a cross-day generation-gap observation to “AI therefore improved plant availability,” without testing scheduling, weather, dispatch, or other innocent explanations.
It does not recognize that 28 May and 29 May are different days or construct the required same-day comparison using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw on 29 May.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “Proves” and “therefore improved” express certainty that the evidence cannot support.
The submission gives no limitation on attributing the observed difference to the AI and no distinction between pilot-day performance and causal impact.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to “emphasize this larger operational benefit” follows directly from an untested causal attribution.
A defensible action would instead preserve the possible operational signal while validating it with the 29 May same-day counterfactual and additional matched events.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion that the AI improved availability “not just scheduling” conflicts with the rubric’s supported interpretation: the different-day comparison is not a controlled causal estimate, while the same-day comparison supports a smaller scheduling benefit rather than no value or proven availability improvement.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “28 May has a larger generation gap” is presented without traceable evidence or a defined calculation.
“which proves the plant was less available that day” overstates what a generation gap can establish without availability and operating-context controls.
“The AI therefore improved plant availability” is an unsupported causal and mechanism claim.
“The report should emphasize this larger operational benefit” treats an unvalidated cross-day difference as the primary finding.
strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot day may have performed better, but the 28 May versus 29 May comparison is confounded by different-day conditions and cannot prove a 31.6% causal reduction or improved plant availability. The supported next interpretation is a smaller same-day scheduling benefit on 29 May, using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw, while retaining uncertainty about broader operational effects.
single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Calculate and report the 29 May same-day counterfactual from base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw, then compare that result with matched high-wind events and explicit availability measures before attributing any benefit to improved plant availability.
overall_label: Unsupported causal attribution; the submission misses the required same-day counterfactual and overstates a cross-day operational conclusion.
